question: What condition of will appears when stirring is absent or incomplete?
premises: Without stirring, the state remains purely supreme.
Will can be devoid of action.
Will can be tinged by what is to be willed.
inference: In the absence of full stirring, will appears either as actionless or as colored by its intended object.
uncertainties: The syntax bridges into the next verse, which names the three resulting states.
plain_english: It is not sufficient; without stirring there remains only the supreme nature. Will may be devoid of action, or it may be tinged by what is to be willed.
